title: Need some fresh eyes on the combat in my isometric ARPG — what would you improve?
author: freesoulapps
selftext:
I’ve been building this isometric sci-fi ARPG for a while now.

A lot of the development is being done with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 agents, and I’m using Meshy for quite a few of the 3D models.

This is the current combat.

I’ve been looking at it for too long at this point, so I’m curious what stands out to fresh eyes.

What looks wrong or weak? What feels missing?

Could be anything — hit impact, enemy reactions, movement, animations, VFX, sound, readability, pacing, camera, whatever.

I’m not really looking for “looks cool”, I’d rather hear what you think needs work.

If you could change 2–3 things first, what would they be?

comments.author: Free-Version-2746
comments.body:
make it turn base.

stand out? nah. it look worse than mobile ads

comments.author: Ok-Pirate5732
comments.body: All of the animations looks quite bad, and it seems like all of the enemies just walk around randomly. Does not look appealing to be honest

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
Thanks, that’s useful. The enemy movement/readability is one of the things I wasn’t happy with either.
When you say the animations look bad, is it mainly the player attacks, enemy locomotion, hit reactions, or basically all of it?

replies.author: slugger1
replies.body:
I find it interesting that most people here either have no eye for even a basic quality bar or are simply satisfied with the current outcome.

Every enemy and the player just kind of waddle around. The movement also looks awkward when sidestepping. The walk animations need more work in general. 

What is going on with the stone-inside-stone inception?

The attack animations need a proper anticipation phase (You can look that up) The dinosaur attack feels weak. The player also seems to have no hit reaction at all.

The world anchoring also looks problematic. For example, the dead dinosaur at 00:15 appears to float above its shadow.

replies.author: pazh1
replies.body:
Yeah its weird to me also, but I get it, sense of accomplishment can really blind you :)  
For op, buy similar game, check its combat, compare one to one, and you will start seeing a lot of issues in your own game.   
List the all wrong things and just iterate slowly, one thing at a time.

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body: Yeah, agreed. The Ascent is actually my main combat reference right now. I think I need to stop judging mine in isolation and start doing direct side-by-side comparisons, movement, attack timing, hit reactions, enemy behavior, VFX and overall weight — and fix the gaps one by one.

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
This is exactly the kind of breakdown I was hoping for, thanks.

I’ve started a dedicated animation pass now, beginning with new player animations using Meshy. After that I’m going through enemy locomotion, sidestepping, attack anticipation, hit reactions and grounding one by one. The floating/anchoring issue you pointed out is a good catch too.

replies.author: Emotional-Cut2952
replies.body: most of these folks are gamers who filter out all the nuances of textures , model detail and animation detail so these vibe coded results probably feel like a big achievement since it's mostly about gameplay for them

replies.author: Ok-Pirate5732
replies.body:
Not trying to be mean but really all of it. Robots just waddling around, the main character holding his gun and shooting from right next to his belly while standing straight up, attacks look like only 5 percent of the animation plays, there's no hit animation, etc. 

There's no excitement or payoff. Even very baseline requirements/standards are missing.

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body: The dinosaurs instantly flipping belly up are sending me LOL

comments.author: Defiant-Balance-7982
comments.body: I guess do a lot of working on your movement animaton. I guess it's why you stood still in the demo but standing still doesn't look fun in any way in the video. Focus on your game play for a while instead of making it look nice.

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body: Thanks, started adding new animations for the player using meshy

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Um.

Surely this is in the earliest possible stage of development, yes? This looks completely unacceptable as an experience. There's no weight to it, there's no sense of excitement, there's barely any motion, everything looks stuff and unresponsive.

I guess I would start with a question: what is your north star for the combat? What is your best case scenario for the experience, do you have example of combat from other ARPGs that are inspirational to you? How do you hope to trade your system for fun to the player?

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body:
The Ascent is probably the closest reference for what I’m aiming at right now. Not trying to copy it exactly, but that kind of weight, responsiveness, readable enemy behavior and punchy isometric combat is the direction.

Most of my work so far went into the underlying game, story/quests, loot, inventory, progression, skill tree, map, enemy systems, etc. Looking at this clip and the feedback here, the combat presentation clearly hasn’t caught up yet.

I’ve started a dedicated pass on it now, beginning with new player animations, then locomotion, attack anticipation, hit reactions, enemy movement and overall impact.

comments.author: bloke_pusher
comments.body: Do me a favor and look at alien shooter 2, that's what I want from an ARPG. Of course, just my taste.

replies.author: freesoulapps
replies.body: Thanks, I’ll check it out. Exactly the kind of concrete reference I was hoping people would suggest.

comments.author: Effective-Map8036
comments.body: art direction needs new uhhhhhhhh direction... we got robots and dinosaurs and horrible 3d isometric views
